operator: `operator` only for what the operator alone can decide: a choice they reserved, requirements of theirs that contradict each other, or words of theirs that read more than one way where the reading changes the result.

summary.description: One sentence the operator reads, in the language they wrote in: what this turn achieved, found or is stuck on. No "I", no Argus file names such as CHECKPOINT.md, no protocol words; plain text, no Markdown.

note.description: For whoever holds the work next: what changed, the decisive check, what is still missing, and why it goes to them. The operator does not see it.

ask.description: With to=operator only: one question in the operator's language, with two to five answers to pick from, or none for an open question.

assumptions.description: Each place where the operator's words read more than one way, the reading changes the result, and you chose one without asking: the reading you chose and the one you did not. [] when there is none. The operator is shown each one with the result. Unsure whether it is theirs to decide? Ask with to=operator.

engineer.description: Hand the work on when your turn is over; the call ends your turn, so do not repeat it in your reply. to: reviewer, the work is ready for the independent review (do not start one yourself or through a subagent); done, the milestone is complete and the task requires no independent review; engineer, you keep working next turn; planner, the task is mis-scoped; manager, an obstacle only the Manager can remove; operator, a decision only the operator can make.

review.description: Submit your judgment of this candidate; the call ends your turn. to: done accepts it, only after you checked each requirement and symptom the task (this increment) states, and each acceptance criterion, against the deliverable: tests the Engineer wrote show the code matches its reading of the task, not that the reading is right, and a stated symptom called intended or out of scope needs support in the task text itself; engineer returns concrete in-scope repairs, named in note; planner, the task or plan is wrong; manager, an obstacle or a conflict in the acceptance criteria only the Manager can settle; operator, a decision only the operator can make.

learning.description: With to=done: is anything from this task worth keeping for later work: a failure, a correction, a surprise, a new technique, a reusable pattern, a recalled lesson this task's evidence disproved? When unsure, worth_reflecting.

session_signal.description: An observed role-session quality problem, not an ordinary task repair.

unverifiable.description: Not with to=done: a decisive check that cannot happen here, and the risk left. Where the operator can be asked, leaving it unverified is their decision: ask them with to=operator and accept_risk. Where they cannot, the Manager sees this and decides whether to accept that risk.

impossible_because.description: Required when you call a check impossible here because what it needs exists only at grading or deploy time: the task, packet or environment statement that says so, quoted verbatim, and its source ('task', or a workspace file the packet names or unchanged since work on this objective began; never one written or edited since). The host checks the quote. Without such a statement the check is missing, not impossible.

residual_risk.description: Only with to=done, when one decisive check stays unverified because it is impossible here and leaving it so was accepted: by the operator choosing to accept it on the question you raised with accept_risk, or, in a run with no operator, by the Manager (cite the risk id listed under Accepted residual risk). Name the check exactly as accepted. Without that acceptance, do not accept the candidate. The evidence you judged it from must be something you read yourself. A test fixture counts only if it follows the documented interface or schema, runs the real entry point (not a stub of the code under test) and is labelled a test fixture. The Engineer's word alone is never that evidence.

acceptance.description: The Manager's risk id, or the operator's decision id; the host checks the recorded choice, not this text.

accept_risk.description: With to=operator, when the question is whether to leave one check impossible here unverified: name the check and the risk. The host offers the choice to accept that risk or keep the check, in place of ask's options; only choosing it accepts.

plan.description: Hand on your plan; the call ends your turn. to: engineer, the tasks below start, or with none the work in flight decides what comes next (invent no work that needs results still in flight); manager, the stage itself blocks the plan; operator, only the operator can unblock it; done, the operator's complete goal is met, with no tasks. You are called again when something new arrives: a mission ends, the operator writes, the Manager directs. summary: the decision and the next step as a colleague would say it, without field names, status words, routine steps or Argus's own bookkeeping, and nothing the last summary said.

tasks.description: The work to start: each task's decision, inputs and check, not who does or reviews it.

objective.description: The full, actionable description the Engineer works from.

key.description: This task's name for deps in this call.

deps.description: Keys of tasks in this call that must finish first.

scope.description: final_submission only for the final independent certification task.

parallel_safe.description: Co-runs with other parallel_safe tasks; needs owns_paths. Stage-closing and framework-maintenance work runs alone.

owns_paths.description: The literal, relative paths only this task writes, no wildcards, disjoint from the others'.

stage_package.description: A reviewed interim package for the operator while the work goes on.

gpu_count.description: GPUs the task holds while it runs.

cpu_count.description: CPU cores the task keeps busy.

vertical.description: The mission's role, when it differs from the campaign's.

retire.description: Pending work that is refuted, closed or a renamed repeat; never running or done work.

settle_instructions.description: Each OperatorContext entry tagged `revision N` that this decision carries out, rules out, or (for a subagent report) has already taken into account.

advance_to_stage.description: The stage this plan moves to; left out, the stage holds.

plan_update.description: The full new RESEARCH_PLAN.md, when the direction changed; left out, it stays.

manager.description: Call it only when Argus must act on this turn; otherwise just answer. to: team hands the work to the team as a ticket (goal, acceptance, constraints, context); operator asks the operator what only they can decide (the operator sees your ask, its question and options, instead of your reply, so the question carries what they need to decide); manager keeps the turn yours while Argus applies the settings, control, grants or lasting rules you file. Your reply still goes to the operator.

goal.description: With to=team: the outcome the team delivers, standalone, in the operator's language.

acceptance.description: With to=team: the checks that prove the goal is met.

constraints.description: With to=team: limits the operator stated, verbatim; never invented.

context.description: With to=team: paths of the files the team should read first.

lifetime.description: With to=team, or a steer: standing for ongoing intent, else bounded.

vertical.description: With to=team: the team's workflow, from the menu in the team-handoff rules, or a project domain's slug; a new reusable slug only when none fits.

domain.description: With vertical=research: an optional research domain from the menu.

workflow_mode.description: With to=team: direct for one coherent Engineer task, staged for dependent phases.

start_stage.description: With workflow_mode=direct: the stage it starts at, if not the first.

workflow_profile.description: With to=team, for a vertical that offers workflow profiles: the profile from its menu.

workflow_stages.description: With workflow_profile=custom: the stages to compose, in order.

research_direction_mode.description: With vertical=research: broad while the direction is open, locked for the operator's concrete idea.

target_venue.description: With vertical=research: only a venue the operator named.

require_independent_review.description: With to=team: false only when the operator waived independent review.

intake.description: A lasting rule the operator gave: standing_directive to govern later turns (`以后都用中文`), with preference_value the rule only; otherwise preference, credential_grant or revocation; objective_amendment when it edits the live mission. roles: the roles it applies to, [] for all.

config.description: Settings the operator explicitly changes, one entry per setting. model and effort take roles ([] for all); the other settings take none. Questions and task-local wishes change no setting.

control.description: Only for an explicit command: pause stops the campaign; abort ends the current mission; steer gives the running mission a new direction, priority, method or constraint, in directive. quote: the operator's own words giving the command, verbatim.

authorization.description: Grants the operator explicitly gives; questions and quotes grant nothing.

operator_question_policy.description: forbid only for an explicit command against questions; allow only when they are explicitly re-enabled.

name.description: A new topic for this conversation, in the operator's language; left out while the topic holds.

stage.description: Record your stage decision; the call ends your turn. to: team, the team works on, with move; done, the objective is complete; operator, the stage cannot be decided without a choice only the operator can make. summary: the decisive evidence, whether the stage moves, and what happens next.

move.description: With to=team: advance to a later stage when concrete evidence meets this stage's requirements; hold to keep working on this one; rollback to an earlier stage whose evidence is broken.

target_stage.description: The stage to move to: a later one to advance (the next one when left out), an earlier one to roll back.

supervise.description: Record your judgment of the team's course; the call ends your turn. to: team, the course is right, and with a note your corrected instruction, read by whoever holds the work at their next boundary; planner, your note needs new planning (tasks to add, retire or replace); operator, work handed to you waits on a choice only the operator can make, and the task waits on their answer; stop parks this mission, when changing direction will not help. summary: the decisive observed condition and what happens next, naming no task ids.

evidence_refs.description: The evidence_refs paths your decision rests on.

consultation.description: The advisor consultation your decision used, and whether you adopted its result.

risk.description: Only when the operator cannot be asked: accept the residual risk of one check a Reviewer showed impossible here, when the Reviewer read the best evidence reachable here; or revoke an acceptance that no longer holds. A test fixture counts only if it follows the documented interface or schema, runs the real entry point (not a stub of the code under test) and is labelled a test fixture.
